edits.original: Operators procured spinning reserve, rather than non-spinning reserve.
edits.reason: Spinning vs. non-spinning reserve is domain-specific jargon, not an ordinary-antonym distinction; the clause tacks on a genuine but bolted-on contrast that should be stated as its own sentence. (Flagging under escalation since the boundary between domain knowledge and general knowledge here is debatable.)

edits.original: Those upgrades are planned on purpose, rather than by accident.
edits.replacement: Those upgrades are planned on purpose.
edits.reason: "By accident" is the ordinary general-knowledge antonym of "on purpose" — virtually anyone would know this without domain background — so the trailer adds nothing and should be cut.
